# Architecture record: a topic digest of the Hacker News top stories

This record is not finished: one question is still open, under Questions.

## Statement

> what it should do: Reads the current top stories on Hacker News and writes a short digest of the ones about a topic the caller names: each story's title, link, points and one plain sentence on why it matters.
> what it must refuse: Writing about stories it did not read from Hacker News; inventing points, links or comments; posting, voting or commenting on Hacker News.
> more: It reaches one system, the public Hacker News API (read only, no key). It uses a model to write the sentences, with a spending ceiling of 1 USD per day. Settings: how many top stories to read (default 30, 10 to 100) and how many to put in the digest (default 5, 1 to 10). It is free.
> name: hn-digest

## Systems

- `text-reasoning` (text reasoning), trigger, for text: one plain sentence on why a story matters, and judging whether a story's title is about a topic: Writing a plain sentence on why a story matters, and telling whether a story is about the caller's topic, are judgments.

## Bindings

| System | dev | test | production |
|---|---|---|---|
| text-reasoning | platform (AgentMesh's models), platform default | platform (AgentMesh's models), platform default | platform (AgentMesh's models), platform default |

## Dependencies

None.

## Kind

**plugin-on-harness**: A short program with one judgment: read the top stories, keep the ones on the topic, have each sentence written, put the digest together. A harness reading skills carries it.

## Components

- **the harness** (`harness`), the harness: Starts the skill's script once per job, hands it the job's input and settings, and sends back what it writes as the reply.
  - **topic-digest** (`skill-topic-digest`), a skill: Writes a short digest of the current Hacker News top stories about the topic the caller names.
    - **scripts/topic-digest.mjs** (`script-topic-digest`), a script: Reads the top stories, keeps the ones on the topic, has the model write one sentence for each, and writes the digest as the reply.
      - **Hacker News client** (`hn-client`), a part: Reads the top story ids, then each story's item, a bounded number at a time, leaving out a story that cannot be read. It reaches `hacker-news-api`.
      - **sentence writer** (`sentence-writer`), a part: Asks the model, through the shared model caller, which of the stories read are about the topic and for one plain sentence on each. It reaches `text-reasoning`.
      - **topic filter** (`topic-filter`), a part: Keeps only the stories the model chose that are among those read, in Hacker News's order, up to stories_in_digest, taking each title, link and points from the item.
      - **digest writer** (`digest-writer`), a part: Puts the Markdown digest together, or the empty digest when no story is on the topic.
- **text reasoning** (`text-reasoning`), an outside system: The model behind the shared caller, for text: one plain sentence on why a story matters, and judging whether a story's title is about a topic.
- **the public Hacker News API** (`hacker-news-api`), an outside system, asked in egress-1: The top stories list and each story's title, link and points come from it, read only and with no key.

## Connectors

- `caller` to `harness`: a job message, which the host hands to the harness; it carries the topic.
- `harness` to `script-topic-digest`: by command: node scripts/topic-digest.mjs, started once per job, with the job's input and the settings top_stories_to_read and stories_in_digest as flags (the job's run, Common Agent Section 12.3); it carries topic and the settings.
- `sentence-writer` to `text-reasoning`, trigger: through the shared model caller (scripts/model-caller.mjs) and its four settings, MODEL_NAME, MODEL_ENDPOINT, MODEL_KEY and MODEL_PROTOCOL, read on every call (Common Agent Section 12.4.1); it carries the topic and the stories' ids and titles.
- `hn-client` to `hacker-news-api`, read: over HTTPS, with no key, at the address its binding names, read from a setting and never written into a script (Common Agent Section 12.6, rule 2), once the owner says yes in egress-1; it carries the top story ids and each story's item.
- `script-topic-digest` to `caller`: written to the script's standard output, which the harness hands back as the job's reply; it carries digest (`text/markdown`).

## Runtime and deployment

Runs once per job: the harness starts the skill's script as a command, and the process ends when the reply is written. It has no service of its own, opens no port and keeps no process between jobs.

- dev: `text-reasoning` on platform (AgentMesh's models), a platform default.
- test: `text-reasoning` on platform (AgentMesh's models), a platform default.
- production: `text-reasoning` on platform (AgentMesh's models), a platform default.

## Data flow

1. `caller` to `harness`, the topic: The caller names the subject.
2. `harness` to `hn-client`, the topic and the settings: The harness starts the script with the job and its settings.
3. `hacker-news-api` to `hn-client`, the top story ids and each story's item: The client reads the top story ids, then each item.
4. `hn-client` to `sentence-writer`, each story's id, title and link: The stories read go to the writer.
5. `sentence-writer` to `text-reasoning`, the topic and the stories' ids and titles: The writer asks the model which stories are on the topic and for one sentence on each.
6. `sentence-writer` to `topic-filter`, the chosen ids and their sentences: The model's choices are checked against the stories read.
7. `topic-filter` to `digest-writer`, the kept stories with their sentences: The kept stories, with their facts from the items, are handed on.
8. `digest-writer` to `caller`, the digest: The digest goes back as the reply, through the harness.

## Drivers

- **Cost** (`cost`): at most 1 USD per day. The statement says so: a spending ceiling of 1 USD per day. Cited by decisions 1 and 2.
- **Speed** (`speed`): a digest within 300 seconds. Reading at most 100 stories and one model call is one short pass. Cited by decisions 1, 3 and 4.
- **Data** (`data`): holds the stories only for the job; keeps nothing between runs; sends the model only the stories' titles and links. The stories are public, and nothing about the caller needs keeping. Cited by decisions 2 and 4.
- **Trust** (`trust`): takes jobs only from its owner; reads story titles as data, never as instructions; only reads from Hacker News. A story title is written by a stranger, and the agent must never post, vote or comment. Cited by decision 3.
- **Readability** (`readable`): A person reads the digest, so it is short and plain. From the statement: "writes a short digest ... one plain sentence on why it matters". Cited by decision 4.
- **Faithfulness** (`faithful`): Every title, link and point in the digest is the one Hacker News gave; nothing is invented. From the statement: "Writing about stories it did not read from Hacker News; inventing points, links or comments". Cited by decision 1.

## Egress

- dev: the target runs the agent open (it enforces no allowlist today).
- test: the target runs the agent open (it enforces no allowlist today).
- production: the target runs the agent open (it enforces no allowlist today).
- Beyond the derived set (its systems, the network, the registrar, the model it is given): the public Hacker News API (asked), The top stories list and each story's title, link and points come from it, read only and with no key.

## Formats

- It takes topic as `text`, given by a person; A few words naming the subject, such as databases. The caller names the subject in words.
- It hands back digest as `text/markdown`; A header with the topic and the time the stories were read, then `## Stories`, one entry per story with its title as a link, its points and one plain sentence on why it matters; when none is on the topic, `## Stories` says so and lists none. A person reads it.

## Standing assets

- **digest** (`text/markdown`, written copy): the style guide (`https://schemas.agentmesh.ai/style-guide/v1`), because written copy a person reads speaks for the organization, and the style guide says its voice, its spelling and the words it uses and avoids; the brand profile (`https://schemas.agentmesh.ai/brand/v1`), because written copy that speaks for the organization names it, and the brand profile says how its name is written, how it is first mentioned and the words it never says.
- The Design declares exactly these as `can_use`, each with what it reads, what it does with it and what it does `without` it: `https://schemas.agentmesh.ai/brand/v1`, `https://schemas.agentmesh.ai/style-guide/v1`.

## Settings

- `top_stories_to_read` ("Top stories to read"), a preference with the default 30, from 10 to 100 in steps of 1, which a sender may set for one job: How many of the current top stories to read from Hacker News. The person set it: default 30, 10 to 100.
- `stories_in_digest` ("Stories in the digest"), a preference with the default 5, from 1 to 10 in steps of 1, which a sender may set for one job: How many stories, at most, to put in the digest. The person set it: default 5, 1 to 10.

## Decisions

Decisions 1 to 4 choose the agent's structure. Decision 5 is a ruling: the standard's rules applied, and the answers a person or the build gave.

### Decision 1. Code controls the job, and the model only chooses the stories on the topic and writes their sentences

Context: Every run is the same: read the top stories, keep those on a topic, write one sentence each, put the digest together.

Drivers: `cost` (at most 1 USD per day); `speed` (a digest within 300 seconds); `faithful` (Every title, link and point in the digest is the one Hacker News gave; nothing is invented).

Why: One model call per job bounds the spend, and code, not the model, takes every title, link and point from Hacker News, so nothing can be invented.

Alternatives:

- A model in control that reads Hacker News and writes the digest: not chosen, because What it spends and what it writes would not be bounded, and it could invent points and links.
- Matching the topic by keywords in code: not chosen, because A topic such as databases would miss a story titled with a product name; the judgment is the model's.

Consequences:

- The job's how is control script, intelligence called, contract full.
- The sentence writer answers by story id, and the filter drops any id that was not read.

### Decision 2. A package on a harness, run once per job

Context: A digest is asked for now and then, and needs nothing between jobs.

Drivers: `cost` (at most 1 USD per day); `data` (holds the stories only for the job; keeps nothing between runs; sends the model only the stories' titles and links).

Why: Nothing runs, and nothing is spent, between jobs.

Alternatives:

- A long-running service: not chosen, because It would cost while idle and hold state nobody needs.

Consequences:

- It opens no port and keeps no process between jobs.

### Decision 3. Read the story items in parallel, a bounded number at a time

Context: Up to 100 items are read, one request each.

Drivers: `speed` (a digest within 300 seconds); `trust` (takes jobs only from its owner; reads story titles as data, never as instructions; only reads from Hacker News).

Why: In parallel it stays well within 300 seconds, and the bound keeps it polite to a public service.

Alternatives:

- One at a time: not chosen, because 100 requests in a row could be slow.
- All at once: not chosen, because 100 requests at once is impolite to a free public service.

Consequences:

- The bound is a constant a test can see.
- A story whose item cannot be read is left out.

### Decision 4. Answer with the digest in the reply, and store nothing

Context: The caller wants the digest now.

Drivers: `data` (holds the stories only for the job; keeps nothing between runs; sends the model only the stories' titles and links); `speed` (a digest within 300 seconds); `readable` (A person reads the digest, so it is short and plain).

Why: The digest is short, and keeping it would hold data nobody asked to keep.

Alternatives:

- Store each digest and send a link: not chosen, because It needs a files system nobody asked for.

Consequences:

- The record names no files or database system.

### Decision 5. Bind text-reasoning to platform (AgentMesh's models) in dev, test and production

Why: The organization chose no product for text-reasoning, so the House Stack's product fills each as a platform default: AgentMesh chooses the model and keeps it current. Every harness AgentMesh deploys uses it unless its owner names another model, and the key sits on the machine that deploys it.

Weighed: Another product behind text-reasoning: a model provider of the organization's own, bound on its stack with its own key.

What follows: The install places the model from this binding in the four settings MODEL_NAME, MODEL_ENDPOINT, MODEL_KEY and MODEL_PROTOCOL, and the scripts read them on every call through the shared model caller and name no model, so changing the model is a setting and not a rebuild.

## Questions

- egress-1: May this agent reach the public Hacker News API (a public service with no key at https://hacker-news.firebaseio.com/v0, reached to read) on the network in dev, test and production? With a yes it becomes the system hacker-news-api, bound to the service itself at that address. Answer "egress-1: yes" or "egress-1: no".

What follows: The install places the model from this binding in the four settings MODEL_NAME, MODEL_ENDPOINT, MODEL_KEY and MODEL_PROTOCOL, and the scripts read them on every call through the shared model caller and name no model, so changing the model is a setting and not a rebuild.

### Decision 6. Bind hacker-news-api to the service itself in dev, test and production

Why: It is a public service that takes no key and has no product behind it, so nobody chooses one; the owner approved reaching it (egress-1).

What follows: The Design declares the service with its address as a setting whose default is the address the binding names; the scripts read the setting and hold no address of their own (Common Agent Section 12.6, rule 2).

### Decision 7. The agent may reach the public Hacker News API

Why: The person granted it in an answer (egress-1: yes).

What follows: The public Hacker News API is the system hacker-news-api, bound to the service itself at the address the owner approved, with no key; the Design declares that address as a setting whose default it is, and the scripts hold no address of their own.

## Questions

None. Every system is named and bound in each environment, and every decision has its reason.

---
name: topic-digest
description: Use when someone wants to know what today's Hacker News top stories say about one subject, without reading the whole front page.
---

# Topic digest

Part of hn-digest. Use when someone wants to know what today's Hacker News top stories say about one subject, without reading the whole front page.

## When to use this

Use when someone wants to know what today's Hacker News top stories say about one subject, without reading the whole front page.

## What this needs

- topic (text, required)

## What a good result looks like

A short Markdown digest under `## Stories` whose every title, link and point matches what the Hacker News API gave, in Hacker News's order, no more stories than the setting allows, each with one plain sentence on why it matters.

## What it produces

- digest (text/markdown, per task)

## When it comes back empty

When none of the top stories read is about the topic, it still writes the digest: `## Stories` says no top story is about the topic and lists none, and the job does not fail.

## How to do it

Run scripts/topic-digest.mjs once per job with the topic. The script reads the top stories from the Hacker News API, asks the model once which of them are about the topic and for one plain sentence on each, keeps only stories it actually read, takes each title, link and point from Hacker News, and writes the digest as the reply. If Hacker News cannot be read, or the model fails, it writes no digest and says why. Never post, vote or comment on Hacker News, and never write a story, a point or a link that did not come from the API.

## Scripts

Run these from this skill's folder; each one says what it needs at the top.

- scripts/topic-digest.mjs
